result: Cavin1 spontaneously assembles into large oligomers containing approximately 50 cavin1 molecules with an apparent diameter of ~60 nm, even in the absence of CAV1. This assembly occurs in both MCF-7 cells (which lack endogenous cavins and caveolae) and in cell-free expression systems.
evaluation: Claims C1, C16, C50, and C51 are well-supported by single-molecule fluorescence analysis showing brightness measurements consistent with ~50 proteins per complex (Figure 1H) and residence time measurements indicating ~60 nm diameter (Figure 1J). The consistency across multiple experimental systems (MCF-7 cells and cell-free expression) strengthens these findings.

result: Cavin2 and cavin3 do not form mixed oligomers with each other, even in the presence of cavin1. Instead, they form mutually exclusive subcomplexes where cavin1 interacts separately with cavin2 or cavin3, but cavin1 does not bridge cavin2 and cavin3 together.
evaluation: Claims C2, C11, C14, and C63 are strongly supported by multiple independent methods: single-molecule coincidence analysis (Figures 2C, 2F, 3A), ALPHAScreen assays (Figures 2H, 2I), pull-down experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), and hypo-osmotic treatment experiments (Figure 4D-F). The convergence of evidence from different techniques provides robust support.

result: Cavin1 forms homo-oligomers and stable heteromeric complexes with both cavin2 and cavin3. The stoichiometry of cavin1-cavin2 oligomers varies continuously with expression levels, while cavin3 incorporation into cavin1 oligomers is limited to approximately 30%.
evaluation: Claims C8-C10 and C52 are supported by single-molecule coincidence analysis in MCF-7 cells (Figures 2A, 2B) and cell-free expression systems with varying DNA ratios (Figures 2D, 2E). The data demonstrate clear homo- and hetero-oligomerization patterns with quantifiable stoichiometries.

result: Hypo-osmotic treatment causes caveolae to flatten and release the cavin coat, which disassembles into stable subcomplexes containing 9 ± 2 cavin molecules with reduced apparent size (~20-30 nm). These subcomplexes remain oligomeric and segregate into separate cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 populations.
evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C19-C21, and C56 are well-supported by single-molecule analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4A-F). The brightness analysis quantifies subcomplex size (Figure 4C), coincidence analysis demonstrates maintained oligomerization (Figure 4B), and segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 is clearly shown (Figure 4F). The data are internally consistent.

result: Cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes form spatially segregated striations on the surface of caveolae. Immuno-EM shows cavin2 and cavin3 localize to the same caveola but with significant spatial separation, while cavin1 and cavin3 show close spatial association without perceivable separation.
evaluation: Claims C5, C24-C27, and C68 are supported by high-resolution immuno-EM (Figure 5A-C) and quantitative Ripley's K function bivariate clustering analysis (Figure 5D) showing significantly lower co-clustering of cavin2-cavin3 compared to cavin1-cavin3. The spatial segregation is consistent with single-molecule fluorescence data and provides structural evidence for distinct subcomplexes.

result: Each caveola contains approximately 3-4 times more CAV1 than cavin1, corresponding to ~140-180 CAV1 molecules and ~40-50 cavin1 molecules per caveola. This ratio is determined by both single-molecule coincidence analysis and brightness measurements.
evaluation: Claims C15, C82, C6, and C80 are supported by single-molecule coincidence analysis (Figure 3B) showing coincidence peak at C=0.25-0.3 and brightness analysis (Figure 3C) showing CAV1 signal 3.5 times brighter than cavin1. The CAV1 stoichiometry (C6, C80) relies on citations to prior work, which is appropriately referenced.

result: When CAV1 and cavin1 are present, cavin2 and cavin3 co-localize on the same caveolae despite not forming direct interactions with each other. The stable cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes come together on the membrane to regulate caveolar structure formation.
evaluation: Claims C18 and C64 are supported by single-molecule analysis showing coincidental diffusion of cavin2 and cavin3 in the presence of CAV1 and cavin1 (Figure 3D), confirmed in both MCF-7 cells and HeLa cells with endogenous proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). The immuno-EM data (Figure 5C) provides structural evidence for co-localization with spatial segregation.

result: Cavin1 oligomer assembly is a very rapid process that occurs within 15 minutes at nanomolar concentrations (<10 nM) in cell-free expression systems, indicating spontaneous assembly at physiologically relevant concentrations.
evaluation: Claims C12 and C53 are supported by real-time observation of cavin1-GFP production in cell-free systems (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) showing formation of large amplitude bursts within 15 minutes at concentrations below 10 nM. This demonstrates the intrinsic propensity for rapid oligomerization.

result: The presence of CAV1 narrows the distribution of cavin1 particle sizes to around 60 nm, corresponding to the typical size of a caveola, without significantly changing the number of cavin1 subunits per assembly.
evaluation: Claim C17 is supported by comparison of size distributions showing CAV1 narrows cavin1 complex size distribution to ~60 nm (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The data demonstrate that CAV1 acts to organize and constrain cavin1 complex size rather than changing oligomer composition.

result: After hypo-osmotic treatment, cavin1-cavin2 subcomplexes have an apparent size of 30 nm while cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes have an apparent size of 20 nm, indicating structural differences between the two types of subcomplexes.
evaluation: Claims C22 and C23 are supported by single-molecule size measurements after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4G) showing distinct size distributions for the two subcomplex types. However, the interpretation assumes spherical geometry, which is acknowledged as a simplification.

result: A typical caveola contains approximately 5 cavin subcomplexes, with each subcomplex potentially composed of three cavin1 trimers (9 cavin molecules total per subcomplex).
evaluation: Claims C54 and C55 are inferred calculations (50 total cavins / 9 per subcomplex ≈ 5 subcomplexes; 9 cavins / 3 per trimer = 3 trimers) based on the experimental data and cited literature on cavin1 trimers. While the arithmetic is sound, the trimer structure is cited from another study (Ludwig et al., 2013) and the calculation assumes uniform subcomplex composition, which may not be accurate given the variable stoichiometries observed.

result: A maximum of approximately 30% of cavin3 can be incorporated into cavin1 oligomers in cell-free co-expression experiments with varying ratios.
evaluation: Claim C13 is supported by cell-free co-expression experiments (Figure 2E) showing limited incorporation of cavin3 into cavin1 oligomers. However, the biological significance of this limitation and whether it reflects in vivo behavior is unclear.

result: After hypo-osmotic treatment, approximately 15% of cavin1-only oligomers are observed in cavin1-cavin2 co-expression and approximately 20% in cavin1-cavin3 co-expression, while all cavin2 and cavin3 remain bound to cavin1.
evaluation: Claims C83 and C84 are supported by single-molecule coincidence analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figures 4D, 4E). The presence of cavin1-only oligomers suggests incomplete saturation or heterogeneity in subcomplex composition.

result: Cavin subcomplexes do not form direct interactions in solution and do not bind strongly on the membrane to form stable mixed structures, as evidenced by complete segregation after release from caveolae.
evaluation: Claims C85 and C86 are supported by the complete lack of co-diffusion between cavin2 and cavin3 after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4F). This suggests weak or absent direct interactions between the subcomplexes, though the inference about membrane binding is more speculative.

result: The stoichiometric ratios determined in this study (CAV1:cavin = 4:1, cavin1:cavin3 = 2:1, cavin1:cavin2 = 2:1 in subcomplexes) are in good agreement with biochemical measurements from Ludwig et al. (2013).
evaluation: Claims C58-C60 appropriately cite prior work and note agreement with current findings. The consistency between independent studies using different methods strengthens confidence in the stoichiometric measurements, though the current study's measurements are more direct.

result: The caveolar coat contains relatively few cavin proteins (~50) compared to other protein coats such as clathrin (~200 subunits), and the mode of assembly is distinct from any other known coat complex.
evaluation: Claims C61 and C72 are supported by the quantitative data on cavin numbers and comparison with established knowledge about clathrin coats. The distinctiveness of the assembly mechanism is a reasonable conclusion based on the observed behavior of pre-formed subcomplexes.

result: The authors propose several speculative models: cavin subcomplexes may pre-assemble in the cytosol and reversibly associate with caveolae; large cavin complexes in the absence of caveolins may be rare in vivo; released subcomplexes could reach distinct cellular destinations; and caveolar properties could be modulated by subcomplex ratios.
evaluation: Claims C57, C65-C67, C69-C71, and C73 are explicitly speculative or hypothetical statements by the authors. While these hypotheses are reasonable interpretations of the data, they require additional experimental validation. The speculation is appropriately qualified in the manuscript but represents future work rather than demonstrated results.

result: Methodological calibrations: GFP to Cherry channel leakage was 10%, GFP monomer residence time was 100 μs, and cavin1 oligomers showed residence times approximately 10 times slower than GFP.
evaluation: Claims C76-C78 describe methodological calibrations that are clearly stated and shown in the data (Figures 1F, 1G, 1I). These are essential technical details for interpreting the single-molecule measurements.

result: CAV1-GFP puncta in the cytoplasm show intensity 150-200 fold higher than single GFP, and cavin1 does not associate with CAV1 in non-caveolar compartments, confirming that observed puncta represent bona fide caveolae.
evaluation: Claims C79 and C81 are supported by brightness analysis (Figure 3C) and citations to prior work establishing the specificity of cavin1-CAV1 association. This provides confidence that the measurements reflect caveolar structures.

result: Background knowledge and established facts about caveolae, caveolins, and cavins from prior literature, including protein characteristics, disease associations, and technical limitations of fluorescent proteins.
evaluation: Claims C28-C49, C62, C74, and C75 represent established knowledge appropriately cited from prior literature or stated as known facts. These provide necessary context for the study but are not novel findings of this work.
